title: Kenyan Caesar Salad
community: Urban Kenya — the restaurant salad standard
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Caesar Salad — crisp romaine lettuce, house-made croutons, shaved parmesan, and a bold Caesar dressing with a Kenyan twist of coriander. Topped with grilled spiced chicken for the complete restaurant version.
longDesc: The Caesar salad has become a staple of Nairobi's restaurant menus — adapted with spiced grilled chicken and fresh coriander for local character. The house-made Caesar dressing, properly made from scratch, elevates this from a side salad to a proper restaurant starter.
steps: Make croutons: toss bread cubes with olive oil and garlic. Bake at 180°C until golden and crunchy.
Make dressing: whisk garlic, lemon, Worcestershire, mustard, and anchovy paste. Gradually whisk in olive oil. Add parmesan, salt, and pepper.
Toss romaine with enough dressing to coat — not drench.
Lay sliced chicken over the top if using.
Drizzle a little extra dressing over the chicken.
chefTips: The dressing should coat the lettuce — not pool at the bottom.
Homemade croutons are dramatically better than commercial ones.
Add the dressing just before serving to prevent wilting.
commonMistakes: Dressing too far in advance — wilted salad.
cookingScience: Caesar dressing is a simple emulsion — the olive oil is gradually added to the acidic base (lemon, Worcestershire) while whisking. The Dijon mustard contains emulsifying compounds that stabilise the oil droplets in the water-based liquid.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan romaine lettuce is grown in highland areas near Nairobi — locally produced.
servedWith: As a starter to any main
healthBenefits: Romaine lettuce provides vitamins A and K.
Olive oil adds healthy monounsaturated fats.
culturalNote: The Caesar salad has become a benchmark of Nairobi's restaurant quality — a simple dish that reveals the kitchen's attention to detail through the quality of the dressing, the freshness of the lettuce, and the crunch of homemade croutons.
